newsitem.title: UK: Arsonists attack fourth N.Irish Catholic church.
newsitem.headline: Arsonists attack fourth N.Irish Catholic church.

text.p: A Roman Catholic church in Northern Ireland was set alight on Tuesday in a growing wave of attacks on churches and community halls by rival pro-British Protestant and Irish Catholic hardliners.
Security sources said the interior of the church in Stoneyford, County Antrim, was badly damaged. It was the fourth Catholic church in the British-ruled province to be torched this month.
Tension has been high for the past year with hostilities by anti-British IRA guerrillas, revenge attacks by Protestant extremists and growing sectarianism.
The Group of 7, comprising Protestant and Catholic business, trade unionists and other leaders in Northern Ireland's economic life on Tuesday voiced concern about the province's political deadlock.
The group said it was "extremely concerned that progress towards peace and stability is so slow".

Peace talks aimed at finding a political settlement in Northern Ireland have been suspended during the May 1 British election campaign but had anyway been heavily bogged down in procedural difficulties.

The Group of 7 statement followed the Irish Republican Army's shooting of a Londonderry policewoman last week and clashes involving a Protestant mob at the weekend which forced eight Catholic families to leave their homes.
Talks between the two communities have failed to defuse tension ahead of the controversial summer marching season by majority Protestants loyal to London.

Pro-British leader David Trimble said on Tuesday he hoped agreement would be reached over a contentious Protestant march at Drumcree, County Armagh, which provoked turmoil across the province last July.
Protestants deny Catholic charges that the parades, accompanied by blaring bands, are displays of pro-British triumphalism.
Trimble, leader of the Ulster Unionist Party (UUP), told reporters he hoped that "this summer will pass off peacefully".
